stories.headline: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark superchip and DGX Station for Windows, reinventing the PC for AI agents

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced RTX Spark at GTC Taipei at Computex on May 31, calling it a 1-petaflop superchip with full CUDA and RTX stack and up to 128GB of unified memory, built in partnership with MediaTek.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA RTX Spark powers the world's first Windows PCs purpose-built for personal agents, featuring 1 petaflop of AI performance, industry-leading power efficiency, full-stack NVIDIA AI and graphics technology, and up to 128GB of unified memory.

key_facts.fact: RTX Spark is an Arm-based chip with 20 CPU cores and 6,144 Blackwell GPU cores, capable of running 120-billion-parameter AI agents locally and 100 fps 1440p gaming, in laptops as thin as 14mm.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia RTX Spark comes with 20 CPU cores (the CPU has been custom-designed by Nvidia and MediaTek) and 6,144 CUDA cores based on Blackwell architecture... can also host 120-billion-parameter AI agents... in a 14mm thick laptop without a power cord plugged in.

key_facts.fact: Over 30 RTX Spark laptops and 10 desktops are coming this fall from Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface, MSI, and Acer; Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra as its flagship.
key_facts.excerpt: Aevermann says Nvidia's partners are already working on over 30 laptops and over 10 desktops, with Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, MSI, and Lenovo all on board for the latter.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also announced DGX Station for Windows, a deskside AI supercomputer powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra superchip with up to 748GB of coherent memory and 20 petaflops of FP4, capable of running 1-trillion-parameter models locally; coming Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today announced NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows... built on the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip... features up to 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of FP4 performance... capable of running frontier AI models of up to 1 trillion parameters locally.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said Microsoft and Nvidia will 'reinvent the PC' in the era of personal AI, with RTX Spark moving the computer 'from tool to teammate' through Windows-native agents.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The PC is being reinvented,' said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. 'For forty years, you launched apps. Click. Type. With RTX Spark and Microsoft Windows, you ask — and the PC does the work.'

sources.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Reinvent Windows PCs for the Age of Personal AI
NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows Puts a Trillion-Parameter AI Supercomputer on Every Enterprise Desk

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Cosmos 3, an open physical AI foundation model, and Isaac GR00T humanoid reference

key_facts.fact: On May 31 Nvidia launched Cosmos 3, an open omnimodel for physical AI built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture that combines vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction across text, image, video, ambient sound, and action.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA today launched NVIDIA Cosmos 3, an open world foundation model for physical AI built on a breakthrough mixture-of-transformers architecture that combines vision reasoning, world generation and action prediction in a single system.

key_facts.fact: Cosmos 3 Super and Cosmos 3 Nano are available now via build.nvidia.com and Hugging Face, with Cosmos 3 Edge coming for real-time inference; Nvidia says it reduces physical AI training and evaluation cycles from months to days.
key_facts.excerpt: Cosmos 3 Super and Cosmos 3 Nano are available now, with Cosmos 3 Edge coming soon for real-time inference... reducing physical AI training and evaluation cycles from months to days.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also unveiled the Isaac GR00T open humanoid reference design powered by its Jetson Thor chip, combining a Unitree H2 Plus robot body with Sharpa five-fingered hands; the company plans to work with humanoid makers in the US, Europe, and South Korea alongside China's Unitree.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia plans to work with humanoid robot makers in the U.S., Europe and South Korea in addition to China's Unitree.

key_facts.fact: A Cosmos Coalition launched alongside the model to advance open world models across industries, with members contributing models, research, and evaluation techniques on Nvidia DGX Cloud infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: The Cosmos Coalition is a global collaboration between world model builders, AI developers and physical AI leaders to advance open world models across industries, enabling members to contribute models, research and evaluation techniques while using Cosmos 3 technologies.

sources.title: NVIDIA Launches Cosmos 3, the Open Frontier Foundation Model for Physical AI
Nvidia to work with US, European humanoid robot makers in addition to China's Unitree

stories.headline: Nvidia ramps Vera Rubin into full production with Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX among first Vera CPU users

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced at GTC Taipei that its Vera Rubin platform is ramping into full production with 150 supply-chain partners in Taiwan across 350+ factories in 30 countries; first systems ship this fall.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Vera Rubin is ramping into full production, with Taiwan's top server makers and global supply chain leaders manufacturing Vera Rubin-based systems at scale... 150 in Taiwan alone — across 350+ factories and 30 countries are ramping Vera Rubin... Production shipments of Vera Rubin are set to begin starting this fall.

key_facts.fact: Vera Rubin delivers 10x agent throughput at scale versus the previous-generation Grace Blackwell platform, unifying NVL72 systems, Vera CPUs, Groq 3 LPX, BlueField-4 STX storage, and Spectrum-6 SPX Ethernet into a single 5-rack 'AI factory' supercomputer.
key_facts.excerpt: Vera Rubin delivers NVIDIA's most extensive POD-scale platform — five purpose-built racks operating as one massive AI supercomputer for agentic workloads... Vera Rubin delivers 10x agent throughput at scale compared with the previous-generation NVIDIA Grace Blackwell platform.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are among the first big users for Nvidia's upcoming Vera CPUs, which Nvidia claims run AI workloads 1.8x faster than competing x86 chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. said Anthropic PBC, OpenAI and SpaceX are among the first big users of its upcoming microprocessor.

key_facts.fact: The Vera Rubin platform introduces Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics, the world's first co-packaged-optics switches with 200Gb/s SerDes, now in production for million-GPU AI factory deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: the Vera Rubin platform introduces NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics, the world's first co-packaged-optics (CPO)-based switches with 200Gb/s SerDes — now in production.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils Agent Toolkit and Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550B-parameter MoE model built for autonomous agents

key_facts.fact: At GTC Taipei Nvidia unveiled its Agent Toolkit: an open suite of models, blueprints and a secure runtime to help developers turn frontier models into long-running, secure AI agents at scale.
key_facts.excerpt: At Nvidia GTC Taipei 2026, concurrent with the Computex conference, the company unveiled the latest iteration of its Agent Toolkit. It's a comprehensive suite of software, open-source models and blueprints for building powerful, long-running digital coworkers.

key_facts.fact: Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for long-running autonomous agents, with up to 5x faster inference speeds and 30% lower running costs versus comparable frontier models in its class, per Nvidia; available June 4 as an NIM microservice via Hugging Face, ModelScope, and OpenRouter.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra, a massive new 550 billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that's built specifically for long-running autonomous agents... up to five times faster inference speeds and 30% lower running costs than comparable frontier models in its class... set to launch on June 4.

key_facts.fact: The core of the toolkit is NemoClaw, a framework providing ready-made templates that structure how agents plan, reason, execute, and delegate tasks; CUDA-X agent skills are available now via the Claude Code marketplace and the Hermes Skills Hub.
key_facts.excerpt: The core of the Agent Toolkit is Nvidia NemoClaw, a new framework that serves as the main blueprint for building agentic orchestration layers... The CUDA-X agent skills are also available now via the Claude Code marketplace and the Hermes Skills Hub.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is also bringing 2x faster local-agent inference across the RTX and DGX lineup via the new OpenShell runtime for Windows and updated llama.cpp/vLLM optimizations, with NemoClaw expanding to all NVIDIA RTX and DGX PCs.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprint is expanding across NVIDIA's full local AI lineup — GeForce RTX, RTX PRO, RTX and DGX Spark, and DGX Station — with new streamlined installers and support for Hermes Agent.

sources.title: Nvidia gives developers the tool to build secure, autonomous AI workers that scale

stories.headline: Shanghai's MiniMax releases M3, a frontier coding-agent model with 1M-token context and open weights coming

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based MiniMax officially released M3 on June 1, a frontier model aimed at developers building coding agents, long-running automation, and multimodal workflows, with a 1-million-token context window and native image and video input.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax has officially released M3, a new frontier model aimed squarely at developers building coding agents, long-running automation and multimodal workflows. The Shanghai AI lab is pitching it as a rare combination: frontier coding performance, a one-million-token context window and native support for image and video input.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax says M3 scores 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, 66.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 34.8% on SWE-fficiency, 28.8% on KernelBench Hard and 74.2% on MCP Atlas, claiming it beats GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on SWE-Bench Pro while approaching Claude Opus 4.7.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax says M3 scores 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, 66.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 34.8% on SWE-fficiency, 28.8% on KernelBench Hard and 74.2% on MCP Atlas. It also says M3 beats GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on SWE-Bench Pro while approaching Claude Opus 4.7.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax says it will publish a technical report and open-source the model weights within 10 days; the model is already available through MiniMax Code, token plans, and API services.
key_facts.excerpt: M3 is available now through MiniMax Code, token plans and API services, while the company says it will publish a technical report and open-source the corresponding model weights over the next 10 days.

key_facts.fact: The company's MiniMax Sparse Attention architecture is said to cut per-token compute at one-million-token context to one-twentieth of the prior generation, with more than 9x faster prefill and 15x faster decoding.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says its MiniMax Sparse Attention architecture cuts per-token compute at one-million-token context to one-twentieth of the prior generation, with more than 9 times faster prefilling and more than 15 times faster decoding.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on January 9, 2026, and is positioning M3 to compete with Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's coding agents, and Google's Gemini developer tools through its MiniMax Code agent product.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on January 9, 2026, according to a Chinasoft International filing... That puts MiniMax in the same strategic lane as Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's coding agents and Google's Gemini developer tools.

stories.headline: Runway picks London as European HQ, pledges $200M+ for UK AI ecosystem by 2028

key_facts.fact: On June 1 Runway told CNBC it will make London its European headquarters and invest more than $200 million in the UK's AI ecosystem by the end of 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Runway, which is building world models, on Monday exclusively told CNBC that the company plans to make London its new European headquarters and will invest more than $200 million into the U.K.'s AI ecosystem by the end of 2028.

key_facts.fact: Runway most recently raised $315 million in a Series E led by General Atlantic with AMD Ventures and Nvidia, at a $5.3 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: The company most recently raised $315 million in a Series E, featuring General Atlantic, AMD Ventures and Nvidia, resulting in a $5.3 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder and co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis cited proximity to UK customers including the BBC, Fremantle, and WPP, along with London's talent pool, as drivers of the choice.
key_facts.excerpt: London 'puts us close to many of our largest European customers already doing serious work with Runway, including BBC, Fremantle and WPP, and it builds on the research team we already have here,' said Anastasis Germanidis.

key_facts.fact: UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan welcomed the move, saying Runway's London hub will bring world-models research to the UK, helping power breakthroughs from film and gaming to science and robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Runway's new London hub will bring pioneering research into world models to the UK, helping power breakthroughs across industries from film and gaming to science and robotics,' Kanishka Narayan, the U.K.'s AI minister, said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: Runway follows Anthropic (April: London office for 800 staff) and OpenAI (its first permanent UK office) in expanding into London, with Google also moving employees into a new UK HQ this summer.
key_facts.excerpt: In April, Anthropic said it's expanding its presence in London with new office space for 800 people, days after rival OpenAI unveiled plans for its first permanent office in the U.K. capital. Google also plans to move employees into a new U.K. headquarters this summer.

sources.title: Nvidia-backed AI company tells CNBC its launching major UK expansion
Runway picks London for its European headquarters with a $200m UK pledge

stories.headline: Beijing's Vast becomes China's newest AI unicorn with ~$200M raise for AI 3D modeling

key_facts.fact: On June 1 Vast, a Beijing-based AI 3D modeling startup founded in 2023 by 29-year-old gamer Simon Song, said it raised nearly $200 million at a valuation above $1 billion, led by Ince Capital and a China Life Insurance-backed venture fund.
key_facts.excerpt: Vast, a 3D-modeling startup founded by a 29-year-old gamer, raised nearly $200 million to become the latest Chinese AI outfit to achieve a valuation of $1 billion. Ince Capital and a venture fund backed by China Life Insurance Co. led the financing.

key_facts.fact: Other investors in the round included Genesis Capital and existing backers Eminence Ventures and Primavera Venture Partners; prior backers include Alibaba and Baidu.
key_facts.excerpt: Other investors in the round included Genesis Capital and existing backers Eminence Ventures and Primavera Venture Partners... The firm — also backed by Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and Baidu Inc.

key_facts.fact: Vast's main product is Tripo Studio, which generates 3D models from text and image prompts for video games, filmmaking, 3D printing, and industrial applications; subscriptions start at $20/month plus per-token usage.
key_facts.excerpt: The firm... develops Tripo Studio, which helps developers and creative professionals generate 3D models from text and image prompts. It charges a monthly subscription starting at $20, plus fees based on token consumption.

key_facts.fact: Vast says it has roughly 20 million users globally — with the bulk in the US, followed by Europe, Japan, and South Korea — and counts NetEase and Sony among its enterprise clients; founder Song says the company could turn a profit within two years.
key_facts.excerpt: The bulk of its 20 million users hail from the US, followed by Europe, Japan and South Korea, founder Simon Song told Bloomberg News. He says Vast could turn a profit within two years.

key_facts.fact: Vast competes with Tencent's Hunyuan 3D and US-based Meshy; Song was a founding member of LLM developer MiniMax before leaving to focus on 3D-asset generation.
key_facts.excerpt: competes with Tencent Holdings Ltd.'s Hunyuan 3D and Silicon Valley startup Meshy... Before that, he was a founding member of large-language-model developer MiniMax Group Inc.
